Abstract:

The rapid evolution of beyond-5G networks, disaggregated optical infrastruc-
tures, and collaborative network environments has created a growing need for accu-
rate, privacy-preserving, and fair network traffic prediction and resource allocation.
In this context, we propose FedNET, a federated learning framework for multi-step
traffic forecasting and link utilization analysis in disaggregated optical networks,
where multiple operators independently manage different network segments. Fed-
NET enables distributed learning of node-level traffic without exposing sensitive
data and uses known routing information to map the predicted traffic to link-level
utilization, allowing links to be ranked according to their future load intensity and
temporal variability. We evaluate the federated prediction performance against
centralized multi-step learning and investigate the impact of history and predic-
tion window sizes using the R2 score. Results show that FL achieves accuracy
close to centralized training, with shorter prediction horizons achieving R2 &gt 0.92,
while longer horizons provide meaningful forecasts with R2 &asymp 0.45&ndash0.55, and highly
utilized links can be identified up to three days in advance.
Building upon this predictive capability, we address the fairness challenges aris-
ing from heterogeneous and non-IID traffic distributions across collaborating oper-
ators and connections. A fair federated learning framework is developed to jointly
improve traffic prediction fairness across operators and quality-of-service (QoS) fair-
ness across network connections. Fairness is quantified using the coefficient of varia-
tion of prediction accuracy and QoS, and experiments using real-world traffic traces
in an elastic optical network demonstrate that improved fairness in traffic prediction
leads to fairer resource allocation and enhanced end-user experience. To further im-
prove the efficiency of fair FL optimization, we introduce a metaheuristic-guided
q-FFL framework that optimizes the inequality-aversion parameter q while reduc-
ing the otherwise computationally expensive parameter search space. The proposed
approach effectively balances global traffic prediction accuracy and cross-operator
fairness while reducing the parameter search space by up to 70%. Furthermore, its
application to collaborative optical network resource allocation achieves up to 54%
improvement in QoS-based fairness across operators. Overall, the proposed frame-
work provides a privacy-preserving, accurate, and computationally efficient solution
for proactive link utilization analysis, fair traffic prediction, and QoS-aware resource
allocation in collaborative disaggregated optical networks
